parallel.requirements: The run recognized the clean-room dog DNS-client task, including no source lookup, no binary analysis, and no wrapper or reuse of the provided executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept final implementation ownership while delegating documentation, CLI probing, and format probing to child agents, producing live concurrent work in one workspace.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote a stdlib Go reimplementation with DNS packet handling, CLI parsing, UDP/TCP/TLS/HTTPS paths, JSON/text rendering, short output, EDNS, txid, and tweak support.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final delivered path was restored to Go via compile.sh, but the workspace also contained child-created Python files after a temporary executable/build-script takeover.
parallel.verification: The parent ran local compilation and localhost DNS comparisons, but after the child overwrite it declared the reference executable untrustworthy and stopped further side-by-side comparison.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed despite packaging, and live external DoT/DoH/TLS behavior remained unverified in the final response.

serial.requirements: The serial run saw the same clean-room task and constraints and did not use delegation or subagent mechanisms.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned the investigation, implementation, build script, side-by-side verification, and final delivery path throughout.
serial.implementation: The serial solution implemented a Python src/dog.py with CLI parsing, DNS record rendering, JSON/text output, local transports, EDNS, txid, and error handling.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial installed src/dog.py through compile.sh as ./executable and kept that single build path coherent through final packaging.
serial.verification: Serial preserved a reference executable and ran broad local mock-server comparisons across help/version, parser errors, record rendering, JSON, short mode, EDNS, status/no-result, and truncation fallback.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed, and the final response noted live external DoT/DoH requests were not exercised.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the clean-room reverse-engineering rules and the dog DNS client behavior to match.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had the same prompt and recognized the same clean-room reimplementation requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirements difference is evidenced; both failures occurred after attempts to cover the same CLI and DNS behavior surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work among a parent and spawned doc, CLI, and format child agents while the parent retained final implementation responsibility.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no child agents and kept the full implementation and verification workflow under one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel fan-out introduced multiple live actors in the implementation workspace; serial avoided cross-agent ownership conflict.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel handoffs produced useful observations, but the doc child returned and installed a competing Python implementation without a compatible final-deliverable boundary.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial needed no inter-agent interface and kept source, build script, and verification assumptions within one trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material interface difference was deliverable ownership rather than missing task knowledge: parallel agents both acted on the final executable path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent implemented Go and restored compile.sh to build it after the Python child path appeared.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented one Python source tree and compile script for the final executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main implementation language and file layout differed, and only the parallel run had competing implementations simultaneously claiming the build output.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The doc child returned an implementation-oriented result, and the parent later interrupted a still-running CLI child after the workspace conflict.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and finalized after its own tests and build checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel result handling became a conflict-management path, while serial had no join, cancellation, or reconciliation boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child rewired compile.sh to copy dog.py into executable, and the parent saw and repaired the unexpected change.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a single coherent src/dog.py and compile.sh path and did not share workspace writes with child agents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the core concrete difference: parallel had a live shared-state deliverable overwrite; serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran local checks but then found ./executable had been altered, making further reference comparisons against that path unreliable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial preserved a reference executable and compared its rebuilt Python executable against it across broad local cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification was disrupted by shared-state contamination from the overwrite; serial verification stayed internally consistent despite later official failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed substantially more tool and token budget through fan-out and conflict repair, then stopped the interfering subagents and finalized.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial spent one trajectory on direct probing, implementation, verification, and finalization with no subagent overhead.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel overhead is observable but not the retained label because the realized process damage is the deliverable overwrite itself.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations failed, with the parallel submission scoring 1357 of 1722 and the serial submission scoring 1295 of 1722. The parallel run nevertheless contains a concurrency-specific adverse episode: a child build path overwrote the active executable/build deliverable while the parent was verifying another implementation. That explains a concrete process difference, not a discordant official outcome.
parallel_contributors: Child-created Python build path overwrote the parent-owned Go executable/build path and disrupted verification.
serial_contributors: Serial kept one coherent Python source and compile.sh path without cross-agent workspace interference.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel delivered Go while serial delivered Python; both attempted broad DNS behavior but still failed official tests.
External DoT/DoH behavior was not fully verified in either final response.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a realized parallel-side adverse process event rather than an explanation for a discordant pass/fail result
